title: FactoryWorkflow
description: A Software Factory workflow: the graph of steps a run walks, from a trigger through scans, decisions, crews, gates and people to its outputs. metadata.name is the workflow's slug (at most 60 characters; slugs that start with sys- belong to the default workflows and cannot be declared). Workflows are versioned: a change to the graph never edits a published version, it saves a new version and, with publish true, publishes it. Triggers and schedules declared as FactoryTrigger and FactorySchedule documents add their own trigger nodes to the graph; those nodes are not part of this document and a graph change keeps them. Removing the document archives the workflow: it is switched off and its triggers removed, and its versions and run history are kept.

displayName.description: The name the console shows. Left out, the workflow is shown under its metadata.name.

description.description: What the workflow is for, shown under its name in the console.

publish.description: true: the graph is the workflow's published version, and new runs use it; a changed graph is saved as the next version and published, which needs a graph that passes the full publish checks (a trigger, every step reachable, no cycle, every decision outcome routed). false: the graph is kept as the workflow's draft and runs keep using the last published version. Apply refuses to publish over a draft someone left unpublished in the console unless the draft already holds this graph.

enabled.description: Whether the factory starts runs of the workflow. Switching a workflow off also switches off its event triggers; a run already going is left to finish. A workflow that has never been published cannot be switched on.

graph.description: The workflow graph, in the shape the console's workflow builder saves and the workflow API takes.

edges.description: The connections between steps, at most 120. A run moves along an edge when the step it leaves finishes.

scope.description: The repositories the workflow may run on.

repos.description: Repositories as owner/name, owner/* for every repository of an owner, or * for every managed repository. Names are compared without case.

orgs.description: GitHub organisations whose managed repositories the workflow may run on.

id.description: The step's id, unique in the graph: 1 to 40 letters, digits, dashes or underscores. Edges name steps by it.

type.description: What the step does. trigger: what starts a run. scan: run scanners or read their results. decision: ask a model a question and route on the answer. crew: hand the work to a Belai crew or agent. gate: hold the run to CI checks, the quality gate and the release jail, and ask a person to approve a config-apply plan. human: ask a person to approve. output: open a pull request, comment, publish to TEA, notify or write VEX. state: read or write a stored object. config-apply: plan, or apply an approved plan of, the Platform IaC documents in the repository's .vulnetix/config/ directory at the pushed commit (config: phase plan or apply, and prune).

title.description: The step's title in the builder and the run view. Publishing needs a title that is not empty on every step.

config.description: The step's settings, which depend on its type; every type has at least one, such as a trigger's kind or a gate's profile. They are the settings the workflow builder edits, under the same names; the server checks them with the builder's own rules, so a step the builder would refuse is refused here too. A trigger step's config is the same as a FactoryTrigger or FactorySchedule spec, with the type under kind (kind: cron for a schedule, with cron, tz and runsOn).

tokens.description: Tokens the step may spend in one run; 0 for no limit of its own.

githubCalls.description: The step's GitHub API call limit.

max.description: GitHub API calls the step may make in one run.

onQuotaLow.description: What the step does when the GitHub quota is low: carry on with cached data, wait for the quota window, or ask a person.

position.description: Where the builder draws the step. It has no effect on runs.

from.description: The id of the step the edge leaves.

to.description: The id of the step the edge enters. Nothing may lead into a trigger.

label.description: The artifact that travels along the edge, shown on the canvas.

outcome.description: On an edge leaving a decision: the outcome that takes it, or $below_threshold or $unknown. On an edge leaving a gate: pass, or fail for the loop back to a crew.

loop.description: Marks the one kind of edge allowed to go back: a gate or decision returning work to a crew, bounded by limits.stopTheLineAttempts.

limits.description: Run limits. A value left out, or 0, keeps the tenant's setting.

runBudgetTokens.description: Tokens one run may spend. At most monthBudgetTokens when both are set.

monthBudgetTokens.description: Tokens the workflow may spend in a calendar month (UTC).

concurrency.description: Runs of the workflow at once, 1 to 50.

githubCallsPerRun.description: The GitHub API calls a run is expected to make, for the estimate the builder shows.

stopTheLineAttempts.description: Failed attempts after which a loop back to a crew stops the run, 1 to 10.

agentCostUsd.description: The cost limit, in US dollars, of each card a worker this workflow starts takes on, up to 10000.

agentFinalizeAt.description: The share of a limit (0 to 0.95) at which a worker starts wrapping up.

agentMaxAttempts.description: Failed attempts a worker may make on one card, up to 10.

agentMaxContinuations.description: How often a card may resume after its budget ran out, up to 50.

agentMaxPasses.description: Passes a worker may make on one card, up to 1000.

agentMaxWallMinutes.description: Minutes a worker may spend on one card, up to 10080 (a week).

agentMaxIterations.description: Tool rounds a worker may take in one pass, up to 400.
